item.title: MLB sets umpiring crews for wild-card series
item.description: Major League Baseball set the umpiring crews for its 2026 wild-card series Monday. Four crews of six were assigned for the best-of-three sets that begin Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Major League Baseball set the umpiring crews for its 2026 wild-card series Monday. Four crews of six were assigned for the best-of-three sets that begin Tuesday. The group is a mix of young and old, with Bill Miller the most decorated as he receives his seventh wild-card assignment. He will serve as one of the four crew chiefs, along with Alan Porter, Mark Wegner and Jordan Baker. Five umpires are making their postseason debuts, and another four are in either their second or third playoff series. The full list, by crew, listed in order from home plate to right field for Game 1: AMERICAN LEAGUE Chicago White Sox at Houston Astros: Alex MacKay, Alex Tosi, Ryan Additon, Alan Porter (CC), Edwin Moscoso, Paul Clemons Boston Red Sox at New York Yankees: Nate Tomlinson, Scott Barry, John Libka, Mark Wegner (CC), John Tumpane, Emil Jimenez NATIONAL LEAGUE Philadelphia Phillies at Atlanta Braves: Dan Merzel, Adam Beck, Mark Ripperger, Jordan Baker (CC), Nestor Ceja, Charlie Ramos Chicago Cubs at San Diego Padres: Ramon De Jesus, Erich Bacchus, Chad Fairchild, Bill Miller (CC), Rob Drake, Clint Vondrak MacKay, Clemons, Jimenez, Ramos and Vondrak are assigned to the postseason for the first time. All but MacKay, who has the plate for White Sox-Astros, will be in right field for their respective Game 1s. --Field Level Media

item.title: Syria says gas pipeline fire between AL-shola and Deir Al-zour caused by "act of sabotage"
item.description: Syria's state petroleum company said a fire broke out on Monday evening on a gas pipeline between the Al-Shola area and Deir Al-Zour after an explosion at a pipeline isolation valve, which it attributed to sabotage, state news agency SANA reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Syria's state petroleum company said a fire broke out on Monday evening on a gas pipeline between the Al-Shola area and Deir Al-Zour after an explosion at a pipeline isolation valve, which it attributed to sabotage, state news agency SANA reported. The fire halted gas flows from the Jbeissa gas plant to power-generation stations, the company said. Fire crews isolated the area on both sides of the blaze and were working to extinguish it as gas pressure fell.

item.title: Knicks, Jalen Brunson ready for next journey after ending title drought
item.description: After the briefest of summer vacations, the New York Knicks are back to work, now with "NBA champions" attached to their name.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: After the briefest of summer vacations, the New York Knicks are back to work, now with "NBA champions" attached to their name. Whether they are called the reigning or defending champions matters little to Jalen Brunson. His focus is on starting anew and getting this team in the right frame of mind for the start of the season. "The way we approached it last year was take it one day at a time every single day. I've talked about certain things. Obviously, we know what it takes, but just go into the same mindset for this journey," Brunson said at the team's media day Monday. "We know it's a new journey, it's a different journey, but the mindset has to be the same, if not better." The journey will not be easy at the beginning. The October schedule includes two games against the Philadelphia 76ers, one against the Boston Celtics and one with the Detroit Pistons, all teams looking to knock off the defending champions. "The first couple weeks of the season is going to show who we are and where we are," Brunson said. The Knicks swept the Sixers in the Eastern Conference semifinals, part of a 12-1 run across the final three series en route to the franchise's first championship in 53 years. The Pistons and Celtics finished ahead of New York (53-29) in the regular-season standings but never faced either in the postseason after Boston fell in the opening round and Detroit lost in the second. Brunson said that communication and accountability remain key to success. "No matter what we're doing, whether we're playing great or we're playing bad, how do we deal with it and learn? We'll hold each other accountable, just like we did last year, and be better," Brunson said. Coach Mike Brown preached something similar. "Upholding our commitment to our standards ... that's not going to change. Our standards are sacrifice, being connected, having a competitive spirit and having a belief in each other in the process. That's our primary focus going into the year. No matter what we accomplished, moving forward, like I said, our standards and how we approach our process is going to be real critical," Brown said. The Knicks brought back almost their entire playoff rotation. The lone exception was backup center Mitchell Robinson, who signed a three-year, $47.4 million contract with the Celtics. His replacement is veteran Andre Drummond, who played for Philly last season. But unity might be elusive if standouts Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart begin to wonder about their futures amid uncertainty about their potential contract extensions. "Winning can either help us or hurt us, but I think we have the personnel and the character to talk with each other and not take things personal when things are said," Brunson said. "It helped us last year and we need to continue that." Brunson said he'll see how his surgically repaired wrist reacts early on. He added that he felt fine playing through the injury in the playoffs. --Field Level Media

item.title: AAR to buy majority stake in aircraft maintenance firm MRO Holdings for $1.8 billion
item.description: Aviation aftermarket services provider AAR said on Monday it would acquire a 65% controlling interest in aircraft maintenance company MRO Holdings for about $1.8 billion.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Aviation aftermarket services provider AAR (AIR.N) said on Monday it would acquire a 65% controlling interest in aircraft maintenance company MRO Holdings for about $1.8 billion. The deal would strengthen AAR's maintenance, repair and overhaul footprint and increase capacity as airlines ramp up demand for aircraft servicing in the face of supply-chain constraints and delays in new jet deliveries. Its shares were up 6% in extended trading. "Through the acquisition of MRO Holdings, we will create the largest heavy maintenance MRO (maintenance, repair, and overhaul) in the world, servicing a combined total of nearly 3,000 aircraft per year in our hangars," said John Holmes, CEO of AAR. MRO Holdings operates aircraft maintenance and modification facilities across the United States, Mexico, El Salvador and Colombia, with about 90% of its revenue coming from sales to US customers. The company is backed by investors including private-equity firm Bain Capital. AAR will have the option to buy the remaining 35% ownership interest of MRO Holdings within six years of the deal's closing. The Wall Street Journal first reported about the deal earlier on Monday, citing people familiar with the matter. AAR expects to fund the transaction through new debt, about $780 million of equity issued to existing MRO Holdings shareholders, and proceeds from a private investment in public equity (PIPE) offering. The transaction is expected to close in AAR's fiscal third quarter ending February 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions.

item.title: Argentina dice iniciará arbitraje contra Reino Unido para detener explotación petrolera en Islas Malvinas
item.description: Argentina dijo el lunes que iniciará un procedimiento de arbitraje internacional contra el Reino Unido si no frena la explotación petrolera en la zona de las disputadas Islas Malvinas mediante el proyecto Sea Lion.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Argentina dijo el lunes que iniciará un procedimiento de arbitraje internacional contra el Reino Unido si no frena la explotación petrolera en la zona de las disputadas Islas Malvinas mediante el proyecto Sea Lion. La medida llega en momentos de [USN:L1N45F0IU TEXT:"tensión"] entre Argentina y el Reino Unido por la disputa de soberanía de las Islas Malvinas, cuyo control está en manos británicas. En un comunicado oficial, el Gobierno indicó que la medida busca impedir la explotación de hidrocarburos en la denominada Cuenca Malvinas Norte y cita el procedimiento de arbitraje previsto por la Convención de las Naciones Unidas sobre el Derecho del Mar. La medida también busca evitar la adopción de nuevas decisiones vinculadas a la explotación de recursos naturales en la Plataforma Continental Argentina. "Si en dos semanas el Reino Unido no frena la explotación ilegítima, vamos a ir al Tribunal Internacional del Derecho del Mar", dijo el presidente libertario argentino, Javier Milei, en su cuenta de X, donde compartió el comunicado. El Gobierno sostiene que Reino Unido lleva adelante un "accionar ilegítimo" en las Islas Malvinas, Georgias del Sur y Sandwich del Sur y en los espacios marítimos circundantes. "La explotación unilateral de los recursos naturales (...) es contraria al derecho internacional y produce un perjuicio irreversible e irreparable a los derechos de soberanía de la República Argentina", indicó. Los propietarios del proyecto Sea Lion, Navitas Petroleum (NVPTp.TA) , de Israel, y Rockhopper Exploration (RKH.L) , del Reino Unido, han dicho que cuentan con licencias válidas del Gobierno de las Islas Malvinas para operar en la zona. El Gobierno dijo que intimó a Londres para que, en un plazo de dos semanas, adopte las medidas necesarias para impedir el inicio o la continuidad de actividades vinculadas con la explotación hidrocarburífera en la plataforma continental argentina. Por otra parte, el Gobierno también denunció vuelos ilegales de la empresa británica THALES UK LIMITED en la ruta aérea entre las Islas Malvinas y Punta Arenas, en Chile, "sin autorización de las autoridades argentinas", y anunció sanciones. Argentina y el Reino Unido pelearon una guerra de dos meses en 1982 por el archipiélago, que culminó con una victoria británica y 649 argentinos y 255 británicos muertos. El Ejecutivo argentino presentó este mes al Congreso un [USN:L1N4590E7 TEXT:"proyecto de ley"] para fortalecer sanciones a empresas que operen en las Malvinas y para crear un Consejo Nacional de Seguridad.

item.title: Burnham offers Britain an 'honest conversation' on tackling problems
item.description: Andy Burnham will offer on Monday an "honest conversation" with Britain to spell out the trade-offs in tackling some of the nation's deepest problems, such as social care and the control of utilities, in his first conference speech as prime minister.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Piper
item.content:encoded: [USN:L8N43L03M TEXT:"Andy Burnham"] will offer on Monday an "honest conversation" with Britain to spell out the trade-offs in tackling some of the nation's deepest problems, such as social care and the control of utilities, in his first conference speech as prime minister. Taking the floor of a vast conference centre in the northwestern English city of Liverpool for his governing Labour Party's annual conference, [USN:L1N43M05W TEXT:"Burnham"] will press his message that his government will end "politics as usual", instead offering Britain hope he believes has long been lost. Yet, Britain's seventh prime minister in a decade will say that underlying his belief that he can restore pride in Britain is a reckoning, one that needs offering a level of honesty "politicians usually avoid". BURNHAM SAYS SOME DECISIONS MIGHT NOT BE POPULAR "We can't carry on as we are. Politics as usual has taken Britain backwards. More of the same isn't good enough and isn't going to get us where we need to be," Burnham will say, according to extracts of his speech provided by his office. "Hope comes from honesty and from saying the things politicians usually avoid." Burnham, a former mayor who replaced [USN:L8N41P1MT TEXT:"Keir Starmer"] as prime minister in July, has come under pressure to offer more detailed plans for government, beyond his initial bid to hand people "breathing space" from cost-of-living pressures. When he came to power, Burnham promised to use his premiership as a "circuit-breaker for Britain", which, like many European countries, has struggled for years with soaring prices and anaemic economic growth. But beyond some immediate measures, including capping bus fares and removing value added tax from electricity bills, his strategy to realise his bigger ambitions to tackle Britain's social care crisis, bring some utilities into public ownership and create more jobs has lacked detail, businesses say. [USN:L6N45J04E TEXT:"On Sunday"], Burnham moved the goalposts for his pledge to do what several other prime ministers have failed to achieve, to tackle the social care system, by saying he would only present his plans at the next national election, due by mid-2029. That offered some relief to a government wanting to avoid the immediate prospect of major tax rises or spending cuts, although Burnham might listen to those arguing for the end of the pensions triple lock, which guarantees that the state pension rises each year by whichever is highest among inflation, wage growth or 2.5%, to fund future social care reform. In a speech his team says will contain a raft of policies and commitments, Burnham is also expected to offer more detail on his pledge for greater public control of energy, water and housing. Saying he initially wanted to give "the usual tub-thumping conference speech", he decided instead to answer a call from those who wanted "less drift and more direction" by setting out "a more serious prospectus for Britain than people have been offered in a generation". "I accept people will not agree with every part of it, but I believe it can turn Britain around," he will say, offering a route to build "a Britain where people feel the country has their back again".

item.title: Pentagon awards RTX's Raytheon $20.7 billion contract for AMRAAM missiles amid stockpile concerns
item.description: The Pentagon awarded RTX's Raytheon business a provisional multiyear contract worth $20.7 billion to accelerate production of AMRAAM missiles, as the military pushes to replenish stockpiles depleted by conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Mike Stone
item.content:encoded: The Pentagon awarded RTX's Raytheon business a provisional multiyear contract worth $20.7 billion to accelerate production of AMRAAM missiles, as the military pushes to replenish stockpiles depleted by conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine. The US has supplied large quantities of weapons to allies while also using munitions in its own military operations in Iran, raising concerns about inventories of key air defense and precision-guided weapons. The AMRAAM is used in air-to-air jet fighter combat as well as in the National Advanced Surface-to-Air Missile System (NASAMS), which is used to defend the Washington area and is used by more than a dozen other countries, including Ukraine, Oman and Qatar. The prospective AMRAAM deal is the latest in a series of large munitions contracts the Pentagon has pursued this year to pressure contractors into ramping output up faster. The award follows a similar pattern to a $58.6 billion Patriot interceptor deal awarded to Lockheed Martin (LMT.N) [USN:L1N43V1N1 TEXT:"in July"], a seven-year procurement plan running through fiscal 2032. As with that contract, industry executives have cautioned that Congress has not yet appropriated the funding needed to support the full multiyear commitment, meaning contractors may be unable to invest at scale in components and facilities until lawmakers act. The production agreements are designed to entice contractors to move faster on increasing output, part of a broader push by the Trump administration to prioritize weapons production over shareholder returns. The contract, if Congress ultimately appropriates the funds, would let RTX continue to invest in its workforce, supply chain and facilities as US demand surges. The company said it nearly doubled AMRAAM production in 2025, compared with the prior year. The deal would be part of the Pentagon's "Arsenal of Freedom" initiative. RTX said earlier this year it would set an annual production goal of at least 1,900 AMRAAM missiles.

item.title: Wembanyama says Finals loss lingers as Spurs eye new season
item.description: Victor Wembanyama said the disappointment of the San Antonio Spurs' NBA Finals defeat by the New York Knicks has lingered into the offseason, with the Frenchman acknowledging he has endured some difficult nights ahead of the new campaign.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Victor Wembanyama said the disappointment of the San Antonio Spurs' NBA Finals defeat by the New York Knicks has lingered into the offseason, with the Frenchman acknowledging he has endured some difficult nights ahead of the new campaign. Wembanyama, speaking at the Spurs' media day on Monday, said he had allowed himself to confront the emotions of losing the [USN:L6N42M021 TEXT:"Finals"] after five games rather than trying to move past them too quickly. "It evolves with time, but I've had a few sleepless nights," the 22-year-old said. "Maybe not sleepless nights, but hard to find sleep sometimes or hard emotions, haunting sometimes." The Spurs' run to the Finals came in Wembanyama's third season, and the 7-foot-4 center said the team was ready to use the disappointment as motivation. "We don't want to hide from anything. We're going to face these emotions," he said. "We're in a great spot. We're very hopeful, very ambitious, and we're ready." Wembanyama signed a [USN:L6N43D003 TEXT:"multi-year contract extension"] with San Antonio in July after averaging career highs of 25 points, 11.5 rebounds and 3.1 assists in 64 regular-season games last season. He became the youngest player to win the NBA's Defensive Player of the Year award and led the league with 3.08 blocks per game.

item.title: Celine Dion brings down the curtain on L'Oreal Paris runway show
item.description: Global beauty brand L'Oreal Paris staged a star-studded runway show in the French capital on Monday, with pop icon Celine Dion making a guest appearance to close out the evening.
item.dc:creator: Dominique Patton
item.content:encoded: Global beauty brand L'Oreal Paris staged a star-studded runway show in the French capital on Monday, with pop icon Celine Dion making a guest appearance to close out the evening. The event held at the start of Paris Fashion Week featured models Kendall Jenner and Heidi Klum, actors Andie MacDowell and Philippine Leroy-Beaulieu, as well as US Olympic skier Lindsey Vonn and Italian Paralympian Beatrice Vio, sashaying down a catwalk against the backdrop of a lit-up Eiffel Tower. Dion, who is in Paris for a [USN:L1N45406R TEXT:"series of concerts"], was a L'Oreal Paris brand ambassador in 2019. L'Oreal Paris is L'Oreal group's (OREP.PA) biggest brand, used by about 600 million consumers, according to the company, and was the biggest contributor to its [USN:L6N43V153 TEXT:"growth"] in the first half of the year. That was largely thanks to new haircare products that are growing four times faster than the market, said Laetitia Toupet, the brand's global president, as well as make-up like its best-selling Infallible 3-second setting spray. "While we are increasingly adopting codes to elevate the brand and make it more luxurious, we always remain close to women around the world," Toupet told Reuters ahead of the event.

item.title: Infantino ordena revisar financiación FIFA, tras solicitud de más reparto de UEFA y CONCACAF
item.description: El presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, ordenó que se evalúen las propuestas para distribuir más fondos a las federaciones nacionales, tras las peticiones de la UEFA y la CONCACAF de que se destinen 2.100 millones de dólares procedentes de las reservas del organismo rector, pero no llegó a comprometer una cantidad concreta.
item.dc:creator: Julien Pretot
item.content:encoded: El presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, ordenó que se evalúen las propuestas para distribuir más fondos a las federaciones nacionales, tras las peticiones de la UEFA y la CONCACAF de que se destinen 2.100 millones de dólares procedentes de las reservas del organismo rector, pero no llegó a comprometer una cantidad concreta. En una carta dirigida a los presidentes de las seis confederaciones continentales, a la que Reuters tuvo acceso el lunes, Infantino dijo que la evaluación se sometería al Consejo de la FIFA el 15 de octubre, y que cualquier financiación extra estaría sujeta a controles financieros y a la aprobación formal. "Hasta que no se haya completado el análisis y las aprobaciones necesarias, ninguna cifra preliminar podrá considerarse un compromiso aprobado para las federaciones miembro", escribió. El presidente de la UEFA, Aleksander Ceferin, y el presidente de la CONCACAF, Víctor Montagliani, propusieron este mes que cada una de las 211 federaciones miembro de la FIFA reciba al menos 10 millones de dólares durante el ciclo 2027-30, además de la financiación para el desarrollo ya existente. Además, pidieron una revisión independiente de las reservas de la FIFA. En su carta del 18 de septiembre, cuestionaban si la propuesta de inversión privada, que la FIFA descartó, había sido necesaria para aumentar la financiación, teniendo en cuenta que, según sus previsiones, las reservas ascenderían a unos 6.000 millones de dólares a finales de 2026. La distribución que proponen mantendría las reservas sobre los 1.500 millones de dólares a lo largo del siguiente ciclo.

item.title: Infantino orders FIFA funding review after UEFA, CONCACAF seek $2.1 billion payout
item.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has ordered an assessment of proposals to distribute more money to national associations, following calls from UEFA and CONCACAF for a $2.1 billion payout from the governing body's reserves, but stopped short of committing to an amount.
item.dc:creator: Julien Pretot
item.content:encoded: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has ordered an assessment of proposals to distribute more money to national associations, following calls from UEFA and CONCACAF for a $2.1 billion payout from the governing body's reserves, but stopped short of committing to an amount. In a letter to the six continental confederation presidents seen by Reuters on Monday, Infantino said the assessment would go before the FIFA Council on October 15, with any additional funding subject to financial checks and formal approval. "Until the assessment and necessary approvals are complete, no preliminary figure can be treated as an approved commitment to the Member Associations," he wrote. UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin and CONCACAF President Victor Montagliani proposed this month that each of FIFA's 211 member associations receive at least $10 million during the 2027-30 cycle, in addition to existing development funding. They also sought an independent review of FIFA's reserves. Their September 18 letter questioned whether FIFA's abandoned private-investment proposal had been needed to increase funding, given reserves they projected at about $6 billion at the end of 2026. They argued their proposed distribution would leave reserves above $1.5 billion throughout the following cycle. Infantino defended the rationale for the withdrawn commercial plan, saying it would have generated funding beyond what FIFA could distribute from existing resources. "The recent commercial proposal, now withdrawn, was intended to enable FIFA to invest more in football – not to replace support that could responsibly be provided from existing resources," he wrote. "So, it would actually have been on top of it." The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was abandoned in July following opposition from confederations, including UEFA, CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation, over a lack of consultation. The dispute has fuelled demands for changes to FIFA's governance. Infantino said FIFA's administration had already been examining how to provide further development and solidarity funding before receiving the confederations' submissions. He asked the confederation chiefs to send their financial models, assumptions and supporting information to the secretary general, with relevant FIFA committees involved in verifying the assumptions. The Council should determine the amount and timing of additional payments, the reserves needed to protect FIFA's obligations and financial independence, and the eligibility, reporting and audit requirements attached to any distribution, he said. The assessment would also consider support for confederations facing demonstrable structural costs. Where sufficient evidence was available, the Council should receive a recommendation on October 15. Otherwise, it should approve “the shortest reasonable timetable” for completing the work. “I will not prejudge the amount. I will support the greatest level of additional funding that can responsibly be delivered through FIFA’s proper governance process, applied fairly and supported by transparent and auditable arrangements,” Infantino wrote. He also reiterated his invitation for proposals to strengthen FIFA's decision-making, while urging the confederation presidents to respect decisions reached through its institutional processes. “Trust is not the absence of disagreement,” he wrote. “It is demonstrated when we engage directly, test proposals against the facts and respect decisions properly reached through FIFA’s democratic and institutional processes – even when the outcome differs from the one we preferred.”

item.title: Papa Leão diz que preocupações com fim do mundo causado pela IA não são “fake news”
item.description: O papa Leão 14 afirmou nesta segunda-feira que as preocupações de que a inteligência artificial possa destruir o mundo não são “fake news” e devem ser levadas a sério, em uma aparente crítica ao presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee
item.content:encoded: O papa Leão 14 afirmou nesta segunda-feira que as preocupações de que a inteligência artificial possa destruir o mundo não são “fake news” e devem ser levadas a sério, em uma aparente crítica ao presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump. O primeiro papa norte-americano, que tem alertado sobre os perigos da IA ao longo de seus 16 meses de papado, também criticou diretamente os CEOs do setor de tecnologia que defendem que não deve haver restrições à tecnologia. “Eu realmente acho que as preocupações levantadas por muitos dos especialistas em IA devem ser levadas a sério”, disse o pontífice em uma coletiva de imprensa durante o voo de volta a Roma, após uma viagem de quatro dias à França. “Não acho que isso seja fake news, como alguns têm dito.” Trump disse à Assembleia Geral da ONU na semana passada que acreditava que os temores sobre os perigos da IA para a humanidade eram uma “farsa”. O papa disse ter lido nesta segunda-feira que o presidente da fabricante de chips Nvidia havia anunciado que poderia haver uma maneira de inserir medidas de segurança em certos modelos de IA. Mas Leão expressou ceticismo, acrescentando: “Ele é o mesmo que, no entanto, diz que não devem ser impostos limites nem haver regulamentação governamental.” O presidente-executivo da Nvidia, Jensen Huang, disse à CBS News neste mês que concordava com Trump de que as preocupações com a segurança em relação à IA eram exageradas. Trump se reunirá com CEOs do setor de tecnologia para discutir inteligência artificial na terça-feira, na Casa Branca. Huang, Mark Zuckerberg, da Meta, Dario Amodei, da Anthropic, e Greg Brockman, da OpenAI, estão entre aqueles que se reunirão com Trump e com o presidente da Câmara dos Deputados, Mike Johnson, segundo fontes a par do assunto. Outros possíveis participantes incluem o presidente-executivo do Google, Sundar Pichai, e o executivo da SpaceXAI, Elon Musk. Johnson disse que as negociações se concentrariam em encontrar um equilíbrio entre inovação e supervisão regulatória e alertou que os EUA correm o risco de perder a corrida da IA para a China se decidirem "hiperregular isso". Leão exortou o mundo a “promover o diálogo, o estudo e a investigação, para encontrar maneiras de garantir que a IA não chegue a um ponto em que possa destruir a humanidade”. “Acho que há pessoas suficientes seriamente interessadas nisso… mas temos que continuar trabalhando”, disse o papa. “Não podemos simplesmente ficar de braços cruzados e fingir que nada vai acontecer.”

item.title: Petróleo fecha em leve alta por preocupações com oferta, enquanto Trump rejeita proposta do Irã
item.description: Os preços do petróleo fecharam em leve alta nesta segunda-feira, em meio a preocupações com as contínuas interrupções no abastecimento, enquanto mediadores do Catar se comprometeram a realizar negociações com os Estados Unidos e o Irã na esperança de chegar a um acordo de paz para reabrir o Estreito de Ormuz.
item.dc:creator: Scott Disavino
item.content:encoded: Os preços do petróleo fecharam em leve alta nesta segunda-feira, em meio a preocupações com as contínuas interrupções no abastecimento, enquanto mediadores do Catar se comprometeram a realizar negociações com os Estados Unidos e o Irã na esperança de chegar a um acordo de paz para reabrir o Estreito de Ormuz. Os preços subiram mais de US$4 por barril no início do pregão, depois que o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, rejeitou uma proposta do Irã que teria reaberto o estreito. Em seguida, o petróleo recuou um pouco, diante das expectativas de que os mediadores do Catar realizariam negociações com ambas as partes. Os contratos futuros do Brent fecharam com alta de 96 centavos, ou 0,9%, a US$105,28 por barril. O petróleo West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dos EUA subiu 19 centavos, ou 0,2%, fechando a US$ 92,60. Espera-se que os mediadores do Catar realizem negociações separadas com o ministro das Relações Exteriores do Irã, Abbas Araqchi, em Nova York, e com a delegação dos EUA na segunda ou na terça-feira, disse à Reuters uma autoridade a par das negociações. Espera-se que as negociações se concentrem em uma versão alterada da proposta de sete dias que o Irã apresentou na semana passada, durante Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas, disse a autoridade, que falou sob condição de anonimato. No fim de semana, o Irã insistiu que somente a diplomacia pode resolver seu conflito com os EUA e Israel, depois que Trump rejeitou a proposta iraniana de reabrir o Estreito de Ormuz e pôr fim às hostilidades. Mantendo aberta a porta para a diplomacia, no entanto, Trump disse à Axios em uma entrevista por telefone no domingo que esperava que os negociadores dos EUA participassem de mais conversas nesta semana. O ministro das Relações Exteriores da Arábia Saudita, o príncipe Faisal bin Farhan, chegou a Washington nesta segunda-feira para conversas com o secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, informou a agência de notícias estatal saudita, em meio à escalada das hostilidades entre Riade e os houthis do Iêmen, apoiados pelo Irã.

item.title: North Korea says US approval for South Korea's nuclear submarine increases regional instability
item.description: North Korea's foreign ministry said in a statement published by state media KCNA that the United States' approval for South Korea's building its first nuclear submarine is "a dangerous development" that added new instability to the political and military environment of the Asia-Pacific region.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: North Korea's foreign ministry said in a statement published by state media KCNA that the United States' approval for South Korea's building its first nuclear submarine is "a dangerous development" that added new instability to the political and military environment of the Asia-Pacific region. The approval is also another demonstration of US nuclear proliferation through AUKUS pact, the North Korean ministry said, outlining a history of what it described as Washington's "radical nuclear arms buildup" that resulted in the "collapse of international nuclear order." South Korea [USN:L1N42305L TEXT:"aims"] to launch its first nuclear-powered submarine by the mid-2030s, under a new programme aimed at countering North Korea's submarine-launched nuclear and missile threats. The plan for Seoul's nuclear submarine was agreed upon with Washington under a [USN:FWN3WP2EM TEXT:"trade deal"] struck between the two allies last year.

item.title: Tunisia’s miserable run continues after Botswana draw in AFCON qualifiers
item.description: Tunisia’s poor form continued as they were held to a 2-2 draw by Botswana in their Africa Cup of Nations Group H qualifier in Rades on Monday, extending their winless run to eight games.
item.dc:creator: Nick Said
item.content:encoded: Tunisia’s poor form continued as they were held to a 2-2 draw by Botswana in their Africa Cup of Nations Group H qualifier in Rades on Monday, extending their winless run to eight games. It is a second successive draw for the North African side at the start of the continental qualifiers having been held to a 1-1 home draw by Uganda on Thursday. Botswana lead the pool with two points from as many matches, the same as Tunisia, while Libya and Uganda have a point each. They meet in Hoima on Tuesday. Thatayaone Kgamanyane put Botswana ahead on 37 minutes but two goals from Hazem Mastouri either side of halftime turned the fixture in the favour of the hosts. But Tunisia were denied victory when Lebogang Ditsele equalised for Botswana on the hour mark and the sparse home crowd left disappointed once again. Yoane Wissa was on target as the Democratic Republic of Congo claimed a 2-1 win over Zimbabwe in Harare to move top of Group E with a full haul of six points. Wissa opened the scoring before turning provider for Samuel Moutoussamy to net a second on the stroke of halftime. Marshall Munetsi scored his third goal in two games late on for the hosts, but the Congolese hung on for the win. Equatorial Guinea defeated Sierra Leone 1-0 in the other match in the group thanks to a strike from Spanish-born forward Loren Zuniga inside the first minute in neutral Yaounde. DR Congo head Group E with six points from their two games, followed by Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea with three each, while Sierra Leone are yet to get off the mark. Burkina Faso moved to the top of Group F as they defeated Central African Republic 1-0 in neutral Casablanca. RB Salzburg teenager Aboubacar Camara scored the only goal of the game on the hour-mark in his second appearance for the senior national team. The top two nations in each pool qualify for the 24-team continental finals that will be staged in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania from June 19 to July 17 next year.

item.title: Reports: Vikings WR Justin Jefferson (ankle) may play Sunday
item.description: An MRI Monday revealed a sprained left ankle for Minnesota Vikings star wide receiver Justin Jefferson, but the two-time first-team All-Pro might suit up for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins, NFL Network and ESPN reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An MRI Monday revealed a sprained left ankle for Minnesota Vikings star wide receiver Justin Jefferson, but the two-time first-team All-Pro might suit up for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins, NFL Network and ESPN reported. In Sunday's 23-16 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the four-time Pro Bowl selection injured his ankle on a 10-yard reception near the end of Minnesota's first possession. He left the field on his own and spent part of the second quarter on the Vikings' sideline, wearing his helmet, before retreating to the locker room. Jefferson, who finished the game with two catches for 32 yards, played in all 17 games for Minnesota in 2024 and 2025. The seven-year veteran missed seven games in 2023 with a right hamstring injury. Through three weeks, Jefferson, 27, has collected 13 receptions for 179 yards and two touchdowns. His departure came on the same day that quarterback Kyler Murray returned to action from a concussion sustained in Week 1. Jefferson's teammate, tight end Josh Oliver, will undergo surgery to repair a torn biceps, ESPN reported Monday. The 29-year-old has three receptions for 46 yards this season, his fourth with Minnesota and eighth in the NFL. --Field Level Media

item.title: Clippers F Brandon Ingram (Achilles, heel) to miss start of season
item.description: Acquired from the Toronto Raptors in the Kawhi Leonard trade earlier this month, two-time All-Star forward Brandon Ingram will miss the start of the Los Angeles Clippers' season while recovering from surgery on his right heel and a partially torn Achilles tendon.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Acquired from the Toronto Raptors in the Kawhi Leonard trade earlier this month, two-time All-Star forward Brandon Ingram will miss the start of the Los Angeles Clippers' season while recovering from surgery on his right heel and a partially torn Achilles tendon. Ingram underwent surgery on his right heel in May, which is when doctors noticed and addressed the Achilles tendon issue, according to Clippers interim president of basketball operations Trent Redden at media day Monday. While there is no timetable set for Ingram's return, Redden said the recovery time for the forward's partially torn Achilles tendon is "about six months less" than if it was fully torn. Ingram, who was acquired along with guard Gradey Dick in the trade, underwent surgery after missing the last two games of Toronto's first-round loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers. "It wasn't until we got our hands on (Ingram) here that we started to see where he was at with his progression," Redden said. "He won't be ready for the start of the season, and we'll reevaluate when we get there." Speaking at media day, the 29-year-old Ingram said his rehabilitation is going smoothly and called his timeline a "week-by-week thing." "I'm doing well in my recovery," the 10-year veteran said. "I'm coming along. I've been in the facility for a little more than a month now. Getting on the court a little bit and getting stronger. "I had been dealing with some pain throughout the year with the Raptors and especially coming down in crunch time. I didn't quite know what it was. Near the end of the season, we figured out what it was. We thought surgery was the best thing to do." Slated to earn $40 million this season, Ingram holds a player option worth $41.9 million for the 2027-28 campaign. Projected to be the revamped Clippers' top scorer once he returns, Ingram is coming off an All-Star season in which he averaged 21.5 points, 5.6 rebounds and 3.7 assists in 77 games for the Raptors. Los Angeles guard Darius Garland is eager for Ingram to return to the court, calling him "super crafty." "Whenever (Ingram) comes back, when he gets out there, I think our pick-and-roll will be the No. 1 thing we go to," Garland said at media day. "I think that can be really nasty." Guard Bradley Beal will not begin training camp on time, Redden said, as the three-time All-Star is dealing with right knee inflammation following left hip surgery. --Field Level Media

item.title: France snatch late winner in Belgium, Italy thrash Turkey 4-1 away
item.description: France substitute Michael Olise scored two minutes from time as the visitors snatched a late 1-0 win against Belgium in the Nations League on Monday, while Italy returned to winning ways with a thumping 4-1 away triumph over Turkey.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gleeson
item.content:encoded: France substitute Michael Olise scored two minutes from time as the visitors snatched a late 1-0 win against Belgium in the Nations League on Monday, while Italy returned to winning ways with a thumping 4-1 away triumph over Turkey. Fortunes ebbed and flowed in Brussels but Olise kept up France coach Zinedine Zidane’s winning start to his new job with a surging run from midway inside the Belgian half before a superb finish to win the Group A1 fixture. France were without captain Kylian Mbappe and Zidane made nine changes to the side that edged Turkey 1-0 last week but it was after bringing on the likes of Ousmane Dembele, Rayan Cherki and Olise that the French turned the game in their favour. “We played a good game, we deserved to win, and we are all relieved by Michael’s goal," said France debutant Lucas da Cunha. "My performance? The coach gave me his full confidence and told me to express myself, to do what I do at club level. I felt good on the pitch." Desire Doue was a persistent danger as he took on the home defence and twice hit the woodwork but Belgium will rue the opportunities they spurned with Mika Godts outstanding for them. "It is a pity, especially because the goal came so late. We created chances ourselves, looked dangerous, and gave very little away. A draw would have been a fairer result," said Belgium centre back Brandon Mechele. Italy lost last Friday’s opening fixture of their Nations League campaign 2-0 at home to Belgium in a false start for Roberto Mancini on his return to the coaching job, but in the rain in Bursa they looked a very different outfit. Alessandro Bastoni gave the visitors a ninth-minute lead from a corner and 13 minutes later Davide Frattesi pounced on a rebound after Michael Kayode’s shot from the left was parried by goalkeeper Altay Bayındır. Italy were 3-0 up in the 27th minute as debutant Kayode hit home a low effort and the visitors finished the half with 10 attempts such was their dominance. FRENETIC GAME IN THE RAIN IN TURKEY The frenetic nature of the game continued after the break as Barıs Alper Yılmaz pulled one back for Turkey, who made three substitutions at halftime, but Italy’s three-goal advantage was restored as Pio Esposito headed home a fourth in the 50th. "The team played well, pressed high, kept possession and played the ball through. We had to focus on this match, which was a difficult one," said Mancini, whose team go to Paris on Friday to face the French. Bosnia registered an emphatic 4-2 win away to Romania in Bucharest in Group B4 as former great Gheorghe Hagi suffered another setback on his return to the manager's post. But Sweden lead the group two points above Bosnia after a second home win, this time 3-1 over Poland in Stockholm. The two Group B2 fixtures ended goalless with Ukraine away in Georgia and Northern Ireland home to Hungary. Montenegro's Aleksa Latkovic scored a last-minute winner as they won 3-2 in Armenia to move three points clear of their opponents on six points atop Group C2 where Latvia and Cyprus drew 0-0 in Riga to each pick up their first point.

Today's Talking Points: AI debt cracks appear US corporate debt markets have been remarkably resilient in the face of soaring Treasury yields and growing concern over AI data center buildout costs. Until now. Cracks are beginning to appear — high-yield spreads broke out on Friday to the widest since April and are approaching 300 basis points, but investment-grade spreads are finally starting to move too. They ended last week at 81 bps, and on Monday likely hit the widest since April. Oracle's debt issues are nothing new, but the blowout in the company's borrowing costs and CDS rates is still remarkable. Meta's bond yields and CDS are also breaking sharply higher. Hyperscalers' bond issuance this year is around $220 billion, and could double next year. It will come at a price, though. An increasingly high price. Another Nvidia record [USN:L6N45K0LY TEXT:"Nvidia"], the world's most valuable company, is boosting its share buyback authorization by a record $150 billion. This brings its remaining buyback capacity to $235 billion, which it expects to deploy through fiscal 2028. It's an extraordinary amount of share-price-boosting firepower, even for a $5.5 trillion market cap entity. Shares bucked the downbeat market on Monday, rising nearly 2%. The buyback move suggests Nvidia thinks its share price should be higher. It's a vote of confidence in the business from the top. As ever with buybacks, however, there's always the nagging doubt that they show a lack of better alternatives. The cold rush Investors are cooling on [USN:L8N45K1C9 TEXT:"gold"]. The yellow metal fell to its lowest in nearly two months on Monday, its 3.5% fall the steepest since early June. Is a break back below $4,000/oz on the cards? It wouldn't be a surprise - the dollar is rising, the Fed seems to be at the beginning of a tightening cycle, and Treasury yields are soaring. None of that is gold-friendly, and US-Iran detente would also dim gold's safe-haven allure. But central banks are sure to be big buyers on dips, if their behavior in recent years is any guide. They have steadily added gold to their reserves, and major holder China is leading the way — Beijing bought 650,000 ounces, nearly 20 tons, in August, the most since October 2023.
